sections.h2: Where Clay County deeds are filed
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is at 261 Courthouse Drive, Suite 2, in Hayesville, or call 828-389-0087. Its website is deeds.claync.us. Your deed to the buyer joins the permanent land record at this office, where the buyer's lender or title attorney can verify it.

Recordable items include deeds, loan documents, cancellations, plats, assumed business names and powers of attorney. The same staff issue marriage licenses, keep vital records and military discharges, and commission notaries.

Staff will not give legal advice, hand out forms, coach drafting, or explain what a recorded paper does to your rights. See a lawyer first.

Clay is a small market of about 12,239 residents and 7,868 housing units. Owner-occupants hold 81.2% of occupied homes, valued at a median $278,400 in the 2020 to 2024 period.

Break the county's layout rules and your deed costs more to file. The real estate records page has the full list.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, printed black on white and blank on the reverse.
  • Page one needs an empty three-inch top margin; keep a quarter inch clear on its other edges and on all edges of later pages.
  • Nothing under 9-point type. Ink is fine for blanks and corrections.
  • The title of the document, for example Deed, stated just beneath the empty band on page one.
  • The signer's signature, plus a notary's seal and acknowledgment.
  • On deeds and loan documents, a "Prepared By" line naming the drafter, the grantee's mailing address, and the excise tax noted on the deed.

Nonconforming paper is still recorded, after the clerk adds a $25.00 non-standard document fee (G.S. 161-10(a)(19)). Correct the margins beforehand and you skip it.

One statewide schedule sets the charges, so Clay matches every other county. Payment is due when you file, so have the office add up your packet before you visit.

What a Clay County seller pays at the Hayesville counter
Document or chargeAmount
Warranty or other deed$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; each page after that adds $4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 covers pages 1 to 35; each page after that adds $4.00
Payoff cancellation of a loan lienFree
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Non-standard document add-on$25.00
Deed excise tax, statute wording$1.00 per $500.00 of price or value, rounding up
Deed excise tax, Clay County wording$2.00 per 1000

Both excise lines describe a single rate in different words.

It falls on the seller, as grantor, and the register holds the deed until it is paid.

Half is kept in Clay County's general fund. The state receives the other half each month, less refunds and the county's allowance. You will find it under seller charges on the settlement statement, because the attorney subtracts it from your proceeds.

G.S. 47-18 says a deed does not protect a buyer from lien creditors or competing purchasers until it is registered in the land's county. Whoever registers first ranks first. Options, contracts to convey, leases longer than three years and rights of first refusal or first offer follow the same rule. A buyer holding an option on Clay County land will want to record it at this office.

Seller financing follows its own chapter. When a one to four family home is sold on a contract for deed, the seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day.

New real property values took effect in 2026. The tax office appeals page says reappraisals run every eight years. The usual sequence is the same each time: review your value notice, ask for an informal review, file a written or in-person appeal if you disagree, then possibly appear before the board. Ask the tax office, not the register, how a new value will change your next bill.

The collector also bills Town of Hayesville taxes. The online payment portal lists a 2.25 percent service fee on credit cards, a $4.95 flat debit fee and a $2.00 electronic check fee.

Bills fall due September 1. A payment made after January 5 picks up interest, 2 percent at first and then three-fourths of a percent for each month starting in February (G.S. 105-360). Make sure whoever runs your closing confirms the bill was paid.

Selling cleanly in Clay County means doing a few things in order. First confirm that the deed on file matches how you hold title and that no paid-off loan is missing its recorded cancellation. Next, a lawyer drafts the deed with a Prepared By line, the buyer's mailing address and the excise tax notation. The signed, notarized deed then goes to Suite 2 with the fee, and the register holds it until the excise tax is paid.

After recording, the time of registration fixes your buyer's priority. Consider keeping a certified copy for your files. Certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page, so a short deed is inexpensive to document. If anything about the recording looks wrong later, the office can pull the record for you.

If you inherited a Clay County house, the paper trail back to the owner who died begins at the superior court clerk's office, well before the register's counter. Inherited property makes up a real share of local sales.

A small estate can be settled by affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1 when personal property, after liens, totals $20,000 or less and 30 days have gone by; a lone surviving spouse can go to $30,000 after any spousal allowance. The affidavit is filed with the clerk in the decedent's home county and has to describe every parcel of land the person held. The state repealed its estate tax, so there is none for deaths since January 1, 2013.

When the clerk's paperwork is in order, the signed deed goes to Suite 2 and is recorded at the table's rates.

From the register's website you can reach online land records and a county fraud-alert service. Sign up, and a notice goes out whenever something new is filed under your name.

Look before you list. Two things can stall a closing: a filing you never signed, and a loan you repaid long ago that nobody cancelled. Satisfactions cost nothing to record, so have the lender file one at payoff. If a house needs fast action, our North Carolina page explains a cash sale option.

faqs.q: Where are Clay County deeds filed?
faqs.a: In Suite 2 at 261 Courthouse Drive, Hayesville, NC 28904, phone 828-389-0087. The deed should follow the office's published margin, type and notary rules.

faqs.q: Will the Hayesville office help me draft a deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft, complete or explain a deed. Hire a lawyer for the drafting.

faqs.q: What if my deed breaks the layout rules?
faqs.a: It is still filed, after a $25.00 non-standard document fee. Fix the margins, type size and notations first to skip the fee.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax my cost as the seller?
faqs.a: Yes. It is paid before filing, at $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or value, counting any part of $500.00 as a full unit.

faqs.q: How often does Clay County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every eight years. New values took effect in 2026, and the tax office can explain what your value means for your bill.
